Background

RestMe began as Restaurant Tamer, a bigger creature-care concept built on Xcode's Game template. Three days into the 10-Day Foundation Challenge, my mentor pushed back: a Game template buries what SwiftUI is actually good at. I rebuilt on the App template instead, embedding SpriteKit through SpriteView, and cut the scope down to one vertical slice, just one creature, one feeding loop, one grill. The outcome is a fire-fox that orders a burger, and a player who has to plate it, cook it, and not miss the green zone before the order times out.

How I Used AI

AI generated background art for the stove, the serve counter, and the dispensers. It also helped me get unstuck on SpriteKit's touch handling and update-loop wiring, the part I struggled with most while turning my mentor's feedback into working code. The assembly order, the grill's Good-divider and Perfect-zone thresholds, what stayed out of this slice, and the game design itself are mine.

Framework

SwiftUI hosts the scene, SpriteKit (through SpriteView) renders it and owns touch, and Combine wires FeedingViewModel's @Published state straight into that layer instead of polling every frame. The ViewModel never imports SpriteKit, so decision logic can't leak into GameScene by accident.
